precepts.text: False brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage: the bondage of the sacrifice system again. Our liberty is that Christ died on the cross; we are free from that burden.
precepts.point: I marvel that ye are so soon removed unto another gospel: which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ. The same men from Acts 15. Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. The gospel they pushed was going back to sacrificing; that is another gospel.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

precepts.why:
“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”. It is not another because it is found in the law of Moses. “but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” They are the same men of Acts 15, who went out from us and troubled the churches. Paul says, if any man preach any other gospel, “let him be accursed”. Those men were running around joining the churches and causing confusion by infiltration, pushing a gospel we are no longer under: going back to sacrificing animals. That is another gospel.

Chapter 2 names them: “And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage”. The liberty we have is that we no longer offer up animals. Christ died on the cross, and we are free from that burden. The bondage they wanted to bring us into was sacrificing animals again to be saved, like Acts 15.

So Galatians 5 says “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.” If animal sacrifice saves you, Christ died for nothing and you are fallen from grace. Yet “ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh”: do not use this freedom to do what you want and sin.

Likewise today, Christians will come in here and do the same thing: accept the identity, but not the theology, using the same book and the same Bible to push Christianity. That is the same infiltration in reverse. As John says, “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and those who trouble you shall bear their judgment.

These Christians use the same scriptures to manipulate people that Jesus is white and it is okay to celebrate Christmas. They were using the same text, but lying with deceitful words. There be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ: that is what the Christian church does today. That is their livelihood.

precepts.why:

Why does it say which is not another? Because the Pharisees were using the same scriptures to manipulate the followers of Christ to go back to animal sacrifice; they said salvation comes through sacrifice. That was the context Paul was dealing with. These Christians use the same scriptures to manipulate people into believing Jesus is white and it is okay to celebrate Christmas. Same text, but lying with deceitful words.

“but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” That is what the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian church does today. They pervert the gospel of Christ; that is their livelihood.

We don't break up families. If your family has no issue with you in the scriptures and isn't trying to manipulate your children, fine. But if your family says, to hell with that Bible, let's smoke some weed and do what we used to do, you had better separate from them. All we can do is warn you.

precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Paul already said how serious it is to bring another doctrine: “But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.” They were coming with a different doctrine than Christ, so let him be accursed.

Then he repeats himself so nobody misses it: “As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.”

That is the weight behind Colossians 2:22. The men teaching the believers to go back to animal sacrifice after Christ were preaching another gospel than the one they had received, and whether it is a man or an angel from heaven, the one who brings it is accursed.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
Paul marvels that they were “so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel”. In Paul's day the Pharisees were deceiving the people to go back to animal sacrifice and give their fealty, their loyalty, to Rome. It is “not another”, because they were using the same scriptures, but “there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ”: the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees and Rome. What is Christianity today? A perversion of the truth of Christ: a white Jesus loved by Negroes and Latinos worshipping their oppressor. You are mad at white folks when they shoot you, then you go to church on Sunday and pray to white folks, and at Christmas and Easter you worship a white man again. It makes no sense.

Isaiah saw it: “Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me”. Praise God, praise Jesus, I love the Lord, yes I does. “but have removed their heart far from me”: you won't do a damn thing, not one law, not one commandment.

“and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”. The white man taught us the Bible. The white man said you don't have to worship God on the Sabbath day, you can do it on Sunday; in fact God is a white man, and anything the white man says is absolute, and Negroes and Latinos bow to that.

So the Lord says “I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.” How? God is raising up the prophets. Christianity will not perish on its own; it perishes through you brothers out there teaching on the streets, doing the videos and the classes seven days a week. The white man they call the wise and prudent man will realize he does not know what he thinks he knows, because the Holy Spirit is in the Israelites, and it is through our teaching that our people are repenting.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
How did “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters” become a scripture used to justify chattel slavery? This is what they did: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.”

That is what Esau did. They took this Bible and perverted it. The servants of Ephesians, Colossians, Peter and Titus were Israelites serving Israelites under the law, hired servants and sojourners who went free in the seventh year and at the jubilee, and whom God said not to rule with rigour. Esau took those scriptures and made them into the slave Bible, to justify ruling over us with rigour in chattel slavery.

And dumb black people, seeing how Esau used them, reject the Bible altogether, not knowing it was perverted.

But God says, “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee”. He gave Egypt for our ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for us, because we are precious in his sight, and he will give men for us. He will bring our seed from the east and gather us from the west, say to the north, give up, and deliver us into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is the true jubilee.

That is what began here, when the scales fell from his eyes and he received sight. Ananias laid hands on him and he was baptized, but Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ taught him directly.

Beyond measure he persecuted and wasted the church of God, profiting in the Jews' religion above his equals and zealous of the traditions of his fathers. This is the man Ananias lays hands on and calls Brother Saul, and the man Christ himself would teach.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul calls himself “an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ”. He was not taught Christ by the disciples and was not awakened by them; Christ himself awakened and taught him. Acts 9 shows the moment. Saul, “yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord”, got letters from the high priest to Damascus so that “if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.”

On the road “suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?” He asked, “Who art thou, Lord?” and the answer was “I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.” Trembling and astonished, Saul asked, “Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?”

Christ himself stopped Paul in his tracks and revealed himself to him even after his death, because Paul played an extremely important role in the gospel. If you are of the elect, if you were commissioned to do a job from the beginning, no matter what point of life you are in, you are going to wake up and fulfill the scriptures.

precepts.point: There are certain people chosen from the foundation of the world to preach this gospel.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
When Ananias hesitated, the Lord said of Saul, “Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

That is Paul's apostleship “by Jesus Christ, and God the Father.” He was a chosen vessel, and his credentials were astounding, above any other person. The things revealed to him were not revealed to many; there were mysteries revealed to him on a level beyond the other disciples, and he was able to go to scriptures and history and show the correlation between the past and the present. There are certain people chosen from the foundation of the world to preach this gospel, and Paul was one of them.

precepts.point: A church just means a gathering or assembly of people. Paul visited Galatia in Acts 16:6 when they went through the region of Galatia, and in Acts 18:23 he went back to strengthen the disciples there.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
The word “brethren” is the key to this verse, and Romans 9 tells who Paul's brethren are. “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises.”

Paul wished he could take on the curses of Christ for his brethren, his kinsmen according to the flesh, meaning according to nationality, according to race, who are Israelites. No other people were called brethren outside of the nation of Israel.

External sources claim the people of Galatia were Gauls or Celts that migrated there, but you must go precept upon precept, line upon line. “And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia” means the churches of Galatia were Israelites congregating.

precepts.point: A church just means a gathering or assembly of people. Paul visited Galatia in Acts 16:6 when they went through the region of Galatia, and in Acts 18:23 he went back to strengthen the disciples there.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
A church just means a gathering or assembly of people, and Paul knew the assemblies of Galatia because he had been there. “Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia.”

That is Paul's visit to Galatia: he went through the region on his journey, and the brethren he writes to, the Israelites congregating in Galatia, are the ones he found there.

precepts.point: A church just means a gathering or assembly of people. Paul visited Galatia in Acts 16:6 when they went through the region of Galatia, and in Acts 18:23 he went back to strengthen the disciples there.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul went back to Galatia a second time. “And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.”

So there were already disciples in Galatia, the churches, the gatherings of Israelites, and Paul returned to strengthen them. Those are the churches of Galatia he addresses with all the brethren who are with him.

precepts.point: This verse also shows that Christ and God are two separate entities: 'Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,' showing they are two separate entities. God is the Father and Christ is the Son of God.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
The grace Paul speaks of is grace and mercy given by Christ. Prior to Christ, under the old covenant, there was no mercy given. “For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.”

That does not mean the law was done away with. The law was also given by Jesus Christ; the only difference is that mercy was given through the blood of Christ. Grace and truth came by him.

The verse also shows that Christ and God are two separate entities: “Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ.” God is the Father and Christ is the Son of God.

precepts.point: When it says 'according to the will of God and our Father,' God refers to Christ (who is called God in Hebrews 1:8) and Father refers to the Most High.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why: Christ “gave himself for our sins.” Whose sins? “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people are the Israelites. So “our sins” means the Israelite sins: Christ gave himself for his people's sins.

precepts.point: When it says 'according to the will of God and our Father,' God refers to Christ (who is called God in Hebrews 1:8) and Father refers to the Most High.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Zacharias confirms who Christ came for: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.” The horn of salvation is Christ from the lion of Judah, raised up in the house of David. He came “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began”: it was prophesied from the beginning of the world for the deliverance of the nation of Israel.

And the purpose: “That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us; To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham, That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear.”

The whole purpose of salvation is to be saved from our enemies, all those who had a hand in our slavery and oppression. That is how Christ delivers us “from this present evil world”: this whole world, this whole system, is based upon sin.

precepts.point: When it says 'according to the will of God and our Father,' God refers to Christ (who is called God in Hebrews 1:8) and Father refers to the Most High.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Christ gave himself “that he might deliver us from this present evil world”, and grace is how that deliverance works in us. “For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world.”

He was the top of his class. His conversation in times past under the law was as a Pharisee, a separated one, of the Pharisaical order.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

Jeremiah 1:5 says the same thing: 'Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee, and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.' Many of us before we came from our mother's womb, the Most High separated us to be prophets. Paul was a minister unto the heathen, meaning the Israelites that were following the customs of other nations.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

points: Paul started preaching the gospel immediately after the spirit of Christ came upon him. He did not go to Jerusalem to consult with the apostles first.

He went into Arabia because there were Israelites living in Arabia, then returned to Damascus where he was confounding the elders, preaching boldly that Christ was the Lord. Acts 9 covers this period.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

points: After three years of teaching, Paul went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and stayed with him fifteen days. The apostles were not aware of what Paul had been doing; he was doing these things having not been taught by Peter and the others.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

points: Paul identifies which apostles he saw when he went to Jerusalem: only Peter and James the Lord's brother. He swears before God that he is telling the truth about his history and his calling.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel
